protocol.validation_scheme: Stratified 5-fold group cross-validation on subject IDs with 5 seeds (42, 123, 456, 789, 1024) and 5 repetitions of the full cross-validation, giving 25 fold-by-seed scores per arm; pairwise comparisons by the corrected resampled t-test (Nadeau and Bengio, 2003), comparisons of three or more arms by the Friedman test with Holm post-hoc, Holm-Bonferroni correction within each experiment, alpha = 0.05, each result reported with its effect size and 95% confidence interval

experiments.title: Hybrid Classification and Fourier Expressivity
experiments.hypothesis: The hybrid architecture combining classical convolutional embedding with circular data re-uploading (L=3, 4 qubits) provides superior non-linear representation compared to single-shot angle encoding and to a classical linear baseline operating on the identical 4-dimensional representation.
experiments.success_criterion: Balanced Accuracy on subject-level test evaluation reaches at least 0.85 and the Hybrid DRU is superior to both single-shot angle encoding and the classical linear probe by the corrected resampled t-test with Holm-adjusted p < 0.05, and non-inferior to EEGNet: the lower one-sided 95% confidence bound of the Balanced Accuracy difference (Hybrid DRU minus EEGNet) lies above -0.03.
experiments.cost: 12 GPU hours on NVIDIA A100 / Tesla T4.

experiments.title: Entanglement Topology Ablation
experiments.hypothesis: Circular CNOT entanglement topology, which entangles every bipartition of the 4-qubit register without making all of them maximally entangled (no 4-qubit state is maximally entangled across its three two-versus-two bipartitions at once, as proposal r04 states), yields higher diagnostic discriminability than linear nearest-neighbor entanglement or separable non-entangled single-qubit rotations.
experiments.success_criterion: Circular entanglement topology demonstrates a higher subject-level F1-score by at least 0.03 compared to the separable non-entangled circuit, with Holm-adjusted post-hoc p < 0.05.

experiments.title: Re-uploading Depth and Barren Plateau Analysis
experiments.hypothesis: Expressivity in the accessible Fourier spectrum increases with re-uploading depth L up to an optimal bound, beyond which gradient variance decays (barren plateau effect) and causes training stagnation or overfitting on validation folds.
experiments.success_criterion: The optimal re-uploading depth L identifies the trade-off point where validation loss reaches a minimum before gradient variance decays by more than one order of magnitude, with the regression slope's 95% confidence interval excluding zero.

experiments.title: Clinical Interpretability via Analytical Gradients
experiments.hypothesis: Analytical gradient saliency derived from the classical backbone and quantum parameter-shift rule concentrates its mass on electrophysiologically relevant fronto-central channels and Theta/Beta frequency components rather than posterior noise.
experiments.success_criterion: The mean per-subject analytical gradient saliency allocated to fronto-central electrode channels (Fp1, Fp2, F3, F4, Fz, Cz) in the Theta and Beta frequency bands is statistically greater (Wilcoxon signed-rank over subjects, Holm-adjusted p < 0.01) than the saliency allocated to posterior temporal-occipital channels.

discussion.summary: Full empirical evaluation of the hybrid quantum-classical neural network with circular data re-uploading (QMLEEG-DRU) across five benchmark experiments (E1-E5). E1 benchmarked 6 arms across 5 folds and 5 seeds (150 models), showing Hybrid DRU achieves 0.683 Balanced Accuracy (0.745 F1, 0.750 AUC), statistically indistinguishable from the Single-shot and Classical Linear baselines (Holm-adjusted p = 1.0), while non-inferiority to EEGNet within the 0.03 margin was not established (one-sided p = 0.382, 95% CI lower bound -0.119); recording duration controls confirm lack of label leakage. E2 demonstrated comparable performance across entanglement topologies (Circular F1 0.745 vs Separable 0.747). E3 confirmed barren plateau gradient variance decay over depth L in {1,2,3,4,6}. E4 established statistically significant fronto-central saliency localization in Theta (p < 0.01) and Beta (p < 0.01) bands conforming to clinical ADHD neuro-biomarkers. E5 validated synthetic capacity and label noise robustness.

metrics.name: Balanced Accuracy
metrics.why: Unbiased performance metric under class imbalance, evaluated at the subject level as the average of sensitivity and specificity across stratified group folds.

metrics.name: F1-score
metrics.why: Harmonic mean of sensitivity and precision across subject-level out-of-fold classifications.

metrics.name: AUC-ROC
metrics.why: Threshold-independent discriminative performance evaluated via DeLong test.

hypotheses.statement: The hybrid architecture combining classical convolutional embedding with circular data re-uploading (L=3, 4 qubits) provides superior non-linear representation compared to single-shot angle encoding and to a classical linear baseline operating on the identical 4-dimensional representation.
hypotheses.test: Friedman across arms followed by Holm-corrected resampled t-test and DeLong test
hypotheses.criterion: Balanced Accuracy on subject-level test evaluation reaches at least 0.85 and the Hybrid DRU is superior to both single-shot angle encoding and the classical linear probe by the corrected resampled t-test with Holm-adjusted p < 0.05, and non-inferior to EEGNet: the lower one-sided 95% confidence bound of the Balanced Accuracy difference (Hybrid DRU minus EEGNet) lies above -0.03.
hypotheses.observed: Hybrid DRU achieved Subject Balanced Accuracy 0.683 (95% CI [0.562, 0.803], F1 0.745), compared to Single-shot (0.708) and Classical Linear (0.689). The strict 0.85 threshold and superiority margin were not met.
hypotheses.rationale: While Hybrid DRU trains stably and achieves 0.745 F1, the empirical subject balanced accuracy of 0.683 does not exceed the pre-specified 0.85 threshold nor reject the null against the comparators at alpha=0.05.

hypotheses.criterion: Circular entanglement topology demonstrates a higher subject-level F1-score by at least 0.03 compared to the separable non-entangled circuit, with Holm-adjusted post-hoc p < 0.05.
hypotheses.observed: Circular topology attained F1 0.745, Linear 0.748, and Separable 0.747. The observed F1 difference was -0.0024 with Holm-adjusted p = 1.0.

novelty.claim: Interleaved classical spatial-temporal feature extraction with quantum data re-uploading circuits for multichannel pediatric EEG classification and exact analytical gradient interpretability.
novelty.rationale: The work provides the first end-to-end benchmark of quantum data re-uploading on a full clinical 120-subject EEG cohort with rigorous non-inferiority comparisons against established deep neural baselines (EEGNet, ADHDeepNet), analytical barren plateau profiling, and electrophysiologically validated gradient topomaps.

qualitative.title: Clinical Saliency Topomap and Biomarker Localization
qualitative.method: Analytical chain-rule gradients backpropagated through classical spatio-temporal layers and quantum parameter-shift circuits
qualitative.reading: Saliency distribution concentrates over fronto-central electrodes (Fp1, Fp2, F3, F4, Fz, Cz) in Theta and Beta bands, matching the pathophysiological neuro-markers of pediatric ADHD rather than temporal-occipital noise.

limitations: Evaluated on state-vector simulation without real quantum hardware noise or shot noise.
Small qubit register (Nq=4) constrained by classical simulation scalability of batch backpropagation.
Pediatric cohort restricted to single recording montage and protocol.
next_steps: Evaluate on physical quantum hardware processors with error mitigation.
Scale to larger qubit registers using tensor network state approximations.

stage_comparison.statement: The hybrid architecture combining classical convolutional embedding with circular data re-uploading (L=3, 4 qubits) provides superior non-linear representation compared to single-shot angle encoding and to a classical linear baseline operating on the identical 4-dimensional representation.

Circular CNOT entanglement topology provides maximum non-local bipartite state connectivity across the 4-qubit register, yielding higher diagnostic discriminability than linear nearest-neighbor entanglement or separable non-entangled single-qubit rotations.

Expressivity in the accessible Fourier spectrum increases with re-uploading depth L up to an optimal bound, beyond which gradient variance decays (barren plateau effect) and causes training stagnation or overfitting on validation folds.

Analytical gradient saliency derived from the classical backbone and quantum parameter-shift rule concentrates its mass on electrophysiologically relevant fronto-central channels and Theta/Beta frequency components rather than posterior noise.

With a fixed feature front end, the re-uploading readout (L=3) represents a class rule that needs Fourier frequency two in one feature, which single-shot angle encoding (L=1) cannot represent; when the class signal is monotone every arm stays close to the known ceiling, and its degradation with the training label-noise rate is measured.
